originalTitle: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom

content: As it prepares to go public, Anthropic’s S-1 filing makes generative AI’s methane dependency glaringly obvious. In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission Monday, Anthropic acknowledges that data centers are becoming increasingly reliant on “natural gas” — the fossil fuel industry’s marketing term for what is primarily methane — leaving the company’s AI data center buildout vulnerable to rising fuel costs and existing supply chain constraints. And in a possible catch-22, Anthropic admits that rising global temperatures — a symptom of burning fossil fuels — will increase the company’s operating costs. “Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense,” Anthropic says, adding that some of its planned data centers rely on electricity generated by natural gas turbines on-site. Anthropic leases capacity from hyperscalers, but it announced a $50 billion dollar plan last year to expand data centers in Texas and New York. The US, the epicenter for data centers globally, is planning to build more fossil fuel generation capacity than it has in a decade as data centers demand more electricity. Donald Trump’s administration has sought to kill renewable energy projects while tilting the regulatory landscape in favor of fossil fuels, which Trump claims is a more important energy source for powering data centers around the clock than solar and wind farms that generate power intermittently. Now, a shortage of gas turbines is slowing data center construction. Some developers are installing gas engines on-site as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to power grids. Developers are also turning to more simple turbine technology at these sites as they face backlogs from turbine manufacturers, making on-site power generation less efficient and more polluting as a result. Data center electricity demand could wipe out decades of gains in air quality over the next five years, one recent Texas-based study found — raising levels of soot, smog-forming pollutants, and planet-heating carbon dioxide. Even as data centers create more greenhouse gas pollution, Anthropic’s S-1 points to climate change as a risk to its bottom line. It will have to pay more for electricity and water to cool servers at data centers as temperatures climb. Nevertheless, Anthropic expects increased competition for natural gas and pipeline capacity from hyperscalers and cloud service providers rushing to build their own data centers. “This competition could drive up the price of natural gas,” the company notes. Gas makes up the biggest chunk of the US electricity mix, 40 percent of the nation’s power generation. And Americans are already feeling the pain of rising costs as utilities scramble to upgrade energy infrastructure and meet rising power demand. Pissed-off residents have successfully blocked dozens of proposed data centers across the US. Anthropic acknowledges that the specter of ballooning utility bills is enough to interfere with a data center project. “If our efforts to secure electrical power are perceived to affect other utility customers and the broader grid, regulators may impose conditions, standby charges, or other requirements intended to address such impacts,” it says. If regulators push data center developers to shoulder more of the costs for new energy infrastructure, Anthropic says that could also raise its operating costs. And without a secure gas supply and the pipelines to transport the fuel, the company says, it might need to delay or abandon planned data center projects altogether. Ultimately, these challenges could stunt Anthropic’s growth: > Any failure to secure access to adequate electrical power, any legal, regulatory, or other administrative action or change limiting the availability of electricity, or any significant increase in energy or compliance costs, could adversely affect our cost structure and limit our ability to scale our compute infrastructure, develop and deploy our models, and service our customers.
chineseTitle: Anthropic 正在燃烧天然气来推动 AI 的繁荣
chineseSummary: 在准备上市之际，Anthropic 的 S-1 文件让生成型人工智能对甲烷的依赖变得显而易见。 “对于获得充足电力供应和数据中心位置的竞争非常激烈。”在周一向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件中，Anthropic 承认数据中心越来越依赖“天然气”[...]
chineseContent: 在准备上市之际，Anthropic 的 S-1 文件让生成型人工智能对甲烷的依赖变得显而易见。在周一向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件中，Anthropic 承认数据中心越来越依赖“天然气”（化石燃料行业的营销术语，主要是甲烷），这使得该公司的人工智能数据中心建设很容易受到燃料成本上涨和现有供应链限制的影响。在可能的第 22 条军规中，Anthropic 承认全球气温上升（燃烧化石燃料的一个症状）将增加公司的运营成本。 Anthropic 表示：“对电力供应和具有充足电力供应的数据中心位置的竞争非常激烈。”他补充说，其计划中的一些数据中心依赖于现场天然气涡轮机产生的电力。 Anthropic 从超大规模企业租赁容量，但去年宣布了一项 500 亿美元的计划，用于扩建德克萨斯州和纽约的数据中心。作为全球数据中心的中心，美国正计划建设比十年来更多的化石燃料发电能力，因为数据中心需要更多的电力。唐纳德·特朗普政府试图扼杀可再生能源项目，同时将监管环境向有利于化石燃料的方向倾斜，特朗普声称，与间歇性发电的太阳能和风电场相比，化石燃料是全天候为数据中心供电的更重要的能源。现在，燃气轮机的短缺正在减缓数据中心的建设。一些开发商正在现场安装燃气发动机，以避免连接电网的漫长等待时间。由于面临涡轮机制造商的积压，开发商也在这些地点转向更简单的涡轮机技术，使得
